task: Stop two gates from turning a git failure into a confident wrong answer. is_safe_file_path silently swapped its path-traversal containment base to the working directory whenever git could not be asked, and three readers in validate_review_marker discarded git's own diagnostic so the ship gate reported a generic cause.

events.content: Issue #3781. get_repo_root returns None for two unrelated reasons: there is no repository, and git could not be asked. is_safe_file_path collapsed both into a fallback to os.getcwd(). The containment check then answered a question nobody asked, namely is this path under the current directory, instead of is this path inside the repository. The false accept is the dangerous half: a process running outside the repo with git failing accepted any path under its working directory.

Considered and rejected three cheaper designs. Failing closed on every None would have broken the legitimate no-repository case that assert_valid_body_file depends on. Walking up for a .git marker would have created a second implementation of git's own discovery rules, a DRY violation in a security path. Logging a warning would have left the false accept in place.

Added resolve_repo_root, which returns (root, reason) with reason in {ok, not-a-repo, git-failed}, and reduced get_repo_root to a one-line wrapper over it. Zero callers change: the None contract is preserved for all 40-odd existing call sites, and only the security check reads the reason.

Discriminating not-a-repo from git-failed uses git's own message rather than a reimplementation of its discovery. Git localizes fatal messages, so the probe pins LC_ALL=C to make the substring deterministic while preserving the rest of the inherited environment. Any failure whose stderr does not carry that message is treated as git-failed, so an unrecognized error fails closed rather than being guessed at.
Verified live before writing tests: inside the repo resolve_repo_root returns (repo path, ok); from a temp directory it returns (None, not-a-repo).

Mutation-tested four guards for #3781. Restoring the conflated fallback fails 1 test, removing the LC_ALL pin fails 2, reading any non-zero exit as not-a-repo fails 2, and reading the exception arms as not-a-repo fails 3. One test I had written, asserting the false-reject case from a subdirectory, survived every mutation because both the old and new code return False there; the fix changes the reason, not the value. It detected nothing, so I deleted it and kept the reasoning in a code comment.

Issue #3782. Overturned the count in the issue body. It says two of three readers discard the diagnostic. Measured: three of four. read_marker_values, read_parent_shas and resolve_tree_sha all drop it; only resolve_sha_with_error preserves it. The third, resolve_tree_sha, feeds the generic message git could not compare commit trees.

Changed all three readers to return (value, error), matching the pattern resolve_sha_with_error already established in the same file, rather than adding a parallel set of _with_error variants. Each reader has exactly one production caller, so the signature change is contained to this module. Added _with_reason to format the outcome message once instead of at four call sites.

Mutation-tested five guards for #3782. Dropping the stderr in each of the three readers fails exactly one test each; making _with_reason never append fails 4; making it append unconditionally fails 1, which is the empty-stderr edge case that would otherwise produce a message ending in a dangling colon.

Re-synced both plugin mirrors. scripts/github_core and scripts/validation/validate_review_marker.py are canonical; scripts/sync_plugin_lib.py propagates to .claude/ and build/scripts/build_all.py propagates on to src/copilot-cli/. Bumped both plugin manifests from 0.6.230 to 0.6.231 and confirmed parity.
